title: Started Learning Java and Spring Boot
body: Revisited Java after several years and began exploring Spring Boot to expand my backend development toolkit beyond Node.js and NestJS. Drawn to its enterprise-oriented architecture and robust ecosystem, I saw this as an opportunity to challenge myself, step outside my comfort zone, and gain experience with a different approach to building scalable, maintainable backend applications.

title: Started Learning ORMs with Drizzle
body: While learning PostgreSQL, I initially focused on writing raw SQL and intentionally avoided ORMs. After discovering Drizzle, I began using it as a way to work with PostgreSQL while continuing to learn the underlying database concepts, including table design, relationships, foreign keys, joins, and how to structure data efficiently.

title: Joined the CS+Social Good Software Engineering Internship
body: Applied for and joined the CS+Social Good software engineering internship, giving me an opportunity to contribute to a real-world project while gaining experience working as part of a software engineering team.

title: Started Graduate Studies at the University of Delaware
body: Began my first semester in the University of Delaware's Computer and Information Sciences graduate program, continuing to develop my software engineering foundation while exploring advanced topics in computer science, algorithms, and systems.

title: Graduated from the University of Delaware
body: Graduated as a first-generation college student with a B.S. in Computer Science. My undergraduate experience gave me a strong foundation in computer science while allowing me to grow through full-stack development, personal projects, and hands-on experience.

title: Accepted into UD's Graduate CIS Program
body: Was accepted into the University of Delaware's Computer and Information Sciences graduate program, giving me the opportunity to continue developing my software engineering skills and explore more advanced areas of computer science.

title: Attended HenHacks for the Second Time
body: Returned to the University of Delaware's HenHacks hackathon for a second time, working with a team to build a full-stack application under a tight deadline. The experience strengthened my skills in rapid development, collaboration, Git, and problem-solving.

title: Deployed My First Full-Stack Monorepo
body: Deployed my first full-stack application using a monorepo architecture, gaining experience organizing and deploying multiple parts of an application within a shared codebase.

title: Adopted NestJS for Personal Projects
body: After learning NestJS in a full-stack software engineering course, I quickly became drawn to its structured and opinionated approach to backend development. I began adopting it in my personal projects, marking my transition away from Express.js.

title: Started Learning NestJS
body: Built a full-stack group expense-splitting application using NestJS, Prisma, and Auth0 for Google authentication. This introduced me to NestJS's structured architecture and strengthened my understanding of building maintainable backend applications.

title: Began My Senior Capstone and Internship Search
body: Started my senior capstone project while searching for internships focused on full-stack software development. I wanted to complement my academic experience with practical experience building software in a professional environment.

title: Shifted Toward Independent Development
body: Began placing greater emphasis on independent development through personal projects and career preparation. This period helped me become more comfortable learning new technologies on my own, solving problems without step-by-step instruction, and consistently building outside the classroom.

title: Deployed My First MERN Application
body: Built and deployed an anonymous note-posting application using the MERN stack and Vercel. This marked my first experience taking a full-stack application from development all the way to production.

title: Adopted Tailwind CSS
body: Moved from vanilla CSS to Tailwind CSS, learning how utility-first styling could speed up development while improving consistency and maintainability across my applications.

title: Attended My First Hackathon: HenHacks
body: Participated in the University of Delaware's HenHacks hackathon for the first time. Working under a tight deadline taught me how to brainstorm, collaborate, use GitHub and branching effectively, and contribute to a shared codebase.

title: Adopted TypeScript
body: Transitioned from JavaScript to TypeScript in my projects, developing a stronger appreciation for type safety, maintainability, and scalability in modern web applications.

title: Started Working in UD's CS Department
body: Became a teaching assistant for the University of Delaware's Computer Science department and joined the Lerner College of Business and Economics Tech Deck as a technical support assistant. These roles strengthened my communication, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills alongside my technical development.

title: Started Learning React
body: Began exploring component-based development with React. Concepts such as state, props, and hooks were initially challenging, but learning how they worked together gave me a much deeper understanding of how modern frontend applications are structured.

title: Started Studying Computer Science at UD
body: Started my Computer Science degree at the University of Delaware, gaining formal exposure to computer science theory, algorithms, data structures, and low-level programming. The coursework challenged me to think beyond simply building applications and gave me a stronger technical foundation.

title: Deepened My MongoDB Knowledge
body: Dove deeper into MongoDB, learning about data modeling, schema design with Mongoose, CRUD operations, and integrating databases into full-stack applications.

title: Explored Full-Stack Development
body: Started combining MongoDB, Express, React, and Node.js to build small applications. This marked the beginning of my transition from learning individual technologies to thinking about how the pieces of a full-stack application work together.

title: Took My First Steps into Backend Development
body: Dove into Node.js and Express and began building APIs, learning how backend services connect frontend applications to databases and other sources of real-world data. This expanded my development experience beyond frontend-focused projects.

title: Accelerated My Learning During the Pandemic
body: Used the pandemic as an opportunity to deepen my JavaScript skills and rebuild my club website from scratch. This period taught me the value of experimentation, iteration, and learning independently.

title: Built My First Major Project
body: Built a website for my high school club using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Firebase. This was my first experience connecting a frontend application to a backend database and gave me my first taste of building something beyond a static website.

title: Started Learning Web Development
body: Began experimenting with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript through YouTube tutorials and simple static websites. This was the beginning of my journey into software development.
